episode.title: Adapt an OpenAI-compatible request boundary to an endpoint that rejects a mirrored reasoning field
episode.before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, endpoint selection had no Fireworks-specific branch, so api.fireworks.ai configurations used the default OpenAI-compatible provider. For model names containing qwen3, that provider copied a non-empty assistant reasoning_content value into reasoning. Replayed thinking history therefore sent both fields to an endpoint reported to reject messages[N].reasoning with HTTP 400.
episode.after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, api.fireworks.ai and its subdomains select a dedicated provider. After applying the default request transformations, that provider immutably removes reasoning only when it is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content, while preserving reasoning_content and any distinct explicit reasoning value. Other endpoints retain the existing default mirroring behavior.
episode.diff: The change adds hostname-based endpoint recognition and provider routing, exports the new adapter, and adds an outbound request normalization override that reverses only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror. New unit tests cover exact and subdomain routing, hostile lookalike hostnames, preservation of distinct explicit values, non-target endpoint behavior, and source-history immutability. An HTTP-backed continuation test exercises conversion, provider normalization, and wire serialization against a strict local endpoint that rejects any assistant reasoning field.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a has parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a and states that the default provider's qwen3 family match mirrors reasoning_content into reasoning, causing Fireworks multi-turn continuation requests to fail with HTTP 400.

The pinned change modifies endpoint/provider selection and exports, adds a dedicated provider implementation, and adds its test suite; the four changed paths are index.ts, provider/index.ts, provider/fireworks.ts, and provider/fireworks.test.ts.
The inherited default request builder mirrors a non-empty assistant reasoning_content string into reasoning for model names containing qwen3 when reasoning is not already a string.

The parent endpoint-selection implementation contains no Fireworks provider import, export, or selection branch and therefore falls through to DefaultOpenAICompatibleProvider after the previously recognized providers.
The new endpoint recognizer parses baseUrl and accepts only the exact api.fireworks.ai hostname or its DNS subdomains, returning false for absent or invalid URLs.

determineProvider now checks the dedicated endpoint recognizer and constructs FireworksOpenAICompatibleProvider before the default-provider fallback; the class is also exported through the provider and content-generator entry points.

The dedicated provider first delegates to the default buildRequest transformations, then maps over the resulting messages and removes reasoning only from assistant messages where reasoning is a string equal to reasoning_content. It creates a replacement message rather than deleting from the input object.

Unit tests assert that exact and subdomain target hostnames suppress the mirrored field while preserving reasoning_content, that source history is not mutated, and that a hostile hostname containing api.fireworks.ai does not select the adapter.

evidence_units.claim: An HTTP-backed test runs two generator turns through session-shaped history, conversion, the dedicated provider, and serialization. Its strict local endpoint returns 400 if any assistant message contains reasoning; the test expects successful continuation, preserved reasoning_content on the wire, and absence of reasoning.

candidate_atomics.name: route_strict_endpoint_to_request_adapter
candidate_atomics.description: Recognize the endpoint by parsed hostname and route it to a provider-specific outbound request adapter without relying on model-family naming.

semantic_action.intent: Apply endpoint-specific request compatibility only to configurations belonging to the strict endpoint, while avoiding accidental adaptation of unrelated services or similarly named models.
semantic_action.module_role: endpoint capability classifier and provider selector
semantic_action.pre_state: The configuration falls through to the generic compatible provider because no endpoint-specific classifier exists; model-family identity alone does not establish endpoint wire capabilities.
semantic_action.post_state: Exact target hostnames and their subdomains select the dedicated request adapter, while invalid URLs, hostile suffix lookalikes, and other endpoints continue through existing selection behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Provider-selection tests exercise the exact hostname, a valid subdomain, a hostile containing hostname, and a non-target endpoint, proving both positive routing and containment of the adaptation boundary.

candidate_atomics.name: remove_only_provider_incompatible_mirror_at_outbound_boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Delegate shared request construction, then immutably remove only the derived duplicate field rejected by the selected endpoint while retaining the canonical replay field and distinct caller data.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent strict-endpoint request rejection without discarding supported reasoning replay data, overwriting explicit caller input, mutating conversation history, or changing other endpoints.
semantic_action.pre_state: The generic request builder has transformed qwen3 assistant history so a non-empty reasoning_content string is also present as an equal reasoning string, but the selected endpoint rejects reasoning as an extra message field.
semantic_action.post_state: For the strict endpoint, assistant messages retain reasoning_content and omit only an equal string-valued reasoning copy; distinct reasoning values, non-assistant messages, source history, and non-target endpoint behavior remain intact.
semantic_action.validation: Focused unit tests verify exact-copy removal, canonical-field preservation, distinct-value preservation, source-history immutability, and unchanged non-target behavior; the HTTP-backed continuation test verifies the normalized wire request is accepted.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_continuation_against_a_strict_wire_contract
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise the real conversion and serialization path against a local endpoint stand-in that rejects the incompatible field, verifying both successful continuation and the exact transmitted message shape.

semantic_action.intent: Demonstrate that provider adaptation resolves the multi-turn continuation failure at the wire boundary rather than only producing the expected in-memory object in an isolated unit.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continued conversation contains a prior model thought that conversion represents as reasoning_content, and the endpoint rejects requests containing assistant reasoning.
semantic_action.post_state: Both turns complete successfully; the continued request carries the prior thought in reasoning_content and sends no assistant reasoning field.
semantic_action.validation: The local HTTP server records request bodies, deliberately responds with the reported 400-shaped error if reasoning is present, and otherwise returns a successful completion; assertions inspect the second recorded body and response.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt_a_shared_request_pipeline_to_a_stricter_compatible_endpoint
candidate_workflows.description: When one nominally compatible endpoint rejects a transformation required by other endpoints, classify that endpoint using a trustworthy endpoint property, reconcile the request after shared transformations, and validate the actual serialized continuation contract while preserving global behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow multi-turn reasoning or tool-call continuation against a stricter compatible endpoint without weakening shared request behavior or losing supported replay data.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A shared provider transformation adds a derived field based on model family, but a particular endpoint rejects that field during replayed multi-turn requests and currently receives the generic provider implementation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The endpoint is narrowly routed to an adapter that removes only the recognizable incompatible derivative at the outbound boundary, preserves canonical and explicit data, leaves other endpoints unchanged, and passes both shape-level and strict wire-contract tests.
unresolved_or_deferred: The bundle contains no issue discussion, review, or CI/status-check evidence, so the endpoint behavior rationale is grounded in the commit message, implementation comments, and executable test oracle rather than independent GitHub discussion.

The checkout working tree was not suitable for executing the added test suite during extraction; validation evidence establishes the committed oracle and assertions, but not a fresh local pass result.
No cross-repository peers or untouched holdout were provided, so this single workflow must not be promoted to a universal resolution pattern.
